chapter: England, Paris and memories of Kansas City and Harlem
title: The Rhythm Club jam session with Louis Armstrong
summary: John Williams took her to the Rhythm Club, where Armstrong, Benny Carter, Hodges and Fats Waller jammed; he made her play. Armstrong was like a god among them.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Do you want to go on with this particular period?
Yes, about the Rhythm Club. I was just talking to Bennie Carter -
I think it was at 132nd and Seventh Avenue in New York.
Oh, maybe '28 or '29. No, '26 or '27. I've forgotten, it was during that time. My husband - he later became my husband - took me in the Rhythm Club, I remember, one night.

John Williams. There was Louis Armstrong, Bennie Carter, Johnny Hodges, Fats Waller, Willie the Lion, and Bennie Carter's cousin that played trumpet. He was just wonderful - I'm trying to think - Cuban Bennett. He was really sensational. He played somewhat like Sweets but all these modern changes and everything. He was just beautiful. Louis Armstrong I mentioned, and J. P. Johnson, and they had this great jam session going. I was hiding practically. My husband says, 'Get up and play.' I said, Oh no,' and I started crying. He says, 'You'd better play.' So I sat down and played with them and I guess they liked it

because they, everybody began hugging and kissing and whatnot. But the thing that impressed me about Louis, I hadn't met him before or heard him play; I had heard about him. He was just like a god among them. When he took his chorus - he had a thing of hitting high notes - they'd say, "Ta-ta, 'yeah,' and the cats in the place, "Ta-ta, 'yeah,' and when he hit the top note everybody would fall out on the floor and scream. It was one of the greatest jam sessions. John Williams used to take me around every night. He'd make me play with all of them.
They had jam sessions like that every night?
Yes, every night, during the day sometimes but the best sessions were at night, where all the greats were. All the great musicians came there.
Did you get used to playing then?
Oh, after while. No, I think each time he had to threaten to hit me or something if I didn't play. I was scared each time.
